salient_findings: Pulsatile mass in the epigastric region
key_facts: 84-year-old man with medical history of hyperlipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, and tobacco use
20-pack-year smoking history
Smoking pipe tobacco for the past 10 years
Asymptomatic abdominal mass with pulsations
Vital signs: Temperature - afebrile, Blood pressure - 120/76 mm Hg, Pulse rate - 73 beats/min, Respiratory rate - 16/minute
Pulses were palpable in the lower extremities bilaterally
Complete blood count and electrolyte levels were within normal limits
Computed tomographic angiogram (CTA) of abdomen and pelvis showed a saccular aneurysm
Aneurysmal neck angulation greater than 60 degrees with neck tortuosity noted
Dense calcifications of iliac vessels present without narrowing
No signs of impending rupture

shortlist.why_kept: Large pulsatile mass in the epigastric region with a soft bruit audible on auscultation and CTA showing a saccular aneurysm

shortlist.label: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large abdominal mass with pulsations and significant displacement of the right ureter

shortlist.label: Aortoiliac occlusive disease
shortlist.why_kept: Dense calcifications of iliac vessels present without narrowing and significant smoking history

shortlist.label: Takayasu arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Large vessel involvement and significant angulation of the aneurysmal neck

shortlist.label: Mycotic aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a saccular aneurysm and potential for infectious etiology given patient's age and comorbidities
